newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault overwhelmed by Scenic's popularity.
newsitem.headline: Renault overwhelmed by Scenic's popularity.

text.p: The popularity of the Megane Scenic, the innovative Renault car designed like a small minivan, has overwhelmed the French automaker which has been forced to delay its launch in Spain and Britain.
"We were expecting a success with the Scenic but not like this. We expected demand to increase gradually, but the response has been immediate," a Renault spokeswoman said on Friday.
Renault, which had planned to launch the Scenic in Britain next month, has delayed its introduction until May, she said. Its launch in Spain has been pushed back five months to June.
The car will be launched on schedule next week in Germany.
Delays in deliveries of the Scenic, voted European Car of the Year in November by top motoring journalists, run to 10 weeks in France, Italy and other countries where it was introduced in the autumn.
The Megane Scenic, which was launched in France in October with a sticker price of 99,700 francs ($18,600), became the top-selling car in its home market in November and December.

Renault has assembled a team to study ways to boost output of the car produced at Renault's factory in Douai. The plant rolls out 700 models a day, while demand is running at around 900-1,000 models daily.
"We're studying more flexible work schedules to produce more cars on the same assembly line," the spokeswoman said.

As the Scenic is built on the same platform as the other Megane cars -- a hatchback and coupe were launched in November 1995 and a four-door sedan was introduced in October -- the company has some scope to adjust production rates of the different models.

Despite the complications resulting from the surge in demand, the Scenic's success is welcome news for Renault, which is the smallest of the Big Six European carmakers and has been losing money on its car operations for more than a year.

Renault, which set a style trend a few years ago with the launch of the whimsical Twingo, conceived the Megane family of mid-sized cars to boost its share of the biggest car market segment in Europe and to diversify sales.
Roughly half the cars it produces are compacts and small cars, which have the slimmest profit margins.

Renault's stock initially shot up one percent to 112.40 francs on Friday morning on a reports of the huge demand for the Scenic. But profit-taking by investors seeking to reduce their holdings in Renault given its poor earnings prospects crushed the rally. The stock closed down 2.34 percent at 108.50 francs.

One stock market analyst said Renault's decision to postpone the British and German launches of the Scenic appeared to be the right move. "If they're doing this to satisfy demand in France, it makes sense because it's in France where they make their biggest profits."

Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer has said the company will probably show a loss for 1996 after losing market share in France and Europe, but he said he was counting on the Meganes to boost sales and earnings this year.
Renault plans to introduce a Megane cabriolet in spring and a stationwagon next year. ($ = 5.349 French Francs)
